lines.text: There are fifty-six ways to walk across this street grid.
lines.caption: There are fifty-six ways to walk across this street grid.

lines.text: Block just one corner, <short pause> and more than half of them vanish!
lines.caption: Block just one corner, and more than half of them vanish!

lines.text: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's solve this together, two different ways.
lines.caption: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's solve this together, two different ways.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: In this street grid, Mia walks from A to B. She goes only right or up, along the streets of the grid.
lines.caption: In this street grid, Mia walks from A to B. She goes only right or up, along the streets of the grid.

lines.text: She does not go through the corner marked X. How many different routes can she take?
lines.caption: She does not go through the corner marked X. How many different routes can she take?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's break it down. The grid is five blocks across and three blocks up.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. The grid is five blocks across and three blocks up.

lines.text: So every route has five right steps and three up steps. That's eight steps in all.
lines.caption: So every route has five right steps and three up steps. That's eight steps in all.

lines.text: Different routes just put those same eight steps in a different order.
lines.caption: Different routes just put those same eight steps in a different order.

lines.text: Here's one route Mia could take. It stays away from X.
lines.caption: Here's one route Mia could take. It stays away from X.

lines.text: This route is not allowed, because it passes through X.
lines.caption: This route is not allowed, because it passes through X.

lines.text: We need to count every route that stays away from X.
lines.caption: We need to count every route that stays away from X.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's write a number on every corner: the number of ways Mia can reach it.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's write a number on every corner: the number of ways Mia can reach it.

lines.text: Along the bottom street, Mia can only walk right. So each corner there gets a one.
lines.caption: Along the bottom street, Mia can only walk right. So each corner there gets a one.

lines.text: Up the left street, she can only walk up. Each corner there gets a one as well.
lines.caption: Up the left street, she can only walk up. Each corner there gets a one as well.

lines.text: Here's the key idea. Mia's last step into a corner comes from the left, or from below.
lines.caption: Here's the key idea. Mia's last step into a corner comes from the left, or from below.

lines.text: So add the number on the left and the number below. One plus one is two.
lines.caption: So add the number on the left and the number below. One plus one is two.

lines.text: Check it: right then up, or up then right. That's two ways!
lines.caption: Check it: right then up, or up then right. That's two ways!

lines.text: Mia can never stand on X, so X gets a zero.
lines.caption: Mia can never stand on X, so X gets a zero.

lines.text: Next to X, zero plus one is one. Then come two and three.
lines.caption: Next to X, zero plus one is one. Then come two and three.

lines.text: Next row up: one plus two is three. Then three plus zero is three.
lines.caption: Next row up: one plus two is three. Then three plus zero is three.

lines.text: Keep going: four, six, and nine.
lines.caption: Keep going: four, six, and nine.

lines.text: The top row gives four, seven, eleven, and seventeen.
lines.caption: The top row gives four, seven, eleven, and seventeen.

lines.text: At B, seventeen plus nine is twenty-six. That's Choice B!
lines.caption: At B, seventeen plus nine is twenty-six. That's Choice B!

lines.text: Now for another method. First count EVERY route, then remove the bad ones.
lines.caption: Now for another method. First count EVERY route, then remove the bad ones.

lines.text: A route is eight steps long, and we only choose which three of them go up.
lines.caption: A route is eight steps long, and we only choose which three of them go up.

lines.text: There are eight choices for the first step that goes up, seven for the second, and six for the third.
lines.caption: There are eight choices for the first step that goes up, seven for the second, and six for the third.

lines.text: But the same three steps get picked in six different orders. So divide by six.
lines.caption: But the same three steps get picked in six different orders. So divide by six.

lines.text: Three hundred thirty-six over six is fifty-six routes in all.
lines.caption: Three hundred thirty-six over six is fifty-six routes in all.

lines.text: Now the bad routes, the ones through X.
lines.caption: Now the bad routes, the ones through X.

lines.text: From A to X is two rights and one up. The up step can be first, second, or third.
lines.caption: From A to X is two rights and one up. The up step can be first, second, or third.

lines.text: That's three ways. From X to B is three rights and two ups.
lines.caption: That's three ways. From X to B is three rights and two ups.

lines.text: Pick two of those five steps to go up. Five times four is twenty, and each pair is counted twice.
lines.caption: Pick two of those five steps to go up. Five times four is twenty, and each pair is counted twice.

lines.text: So that's ten ways to finish. Each of the three starts goes with each of the ten finishes.
lines.caption: So that's ten ways to finish. Each of the three starts goes with each of the ten finishes.

lines.text: Why multiply? Every start can be paired with every finish.
lines.caption: Why multiply? Every start can be paired with every finish.

lines.text: Three times ten is thirty routes through X. Fifty-six minus thirty is twenty-six. It matches!
lines.caption: Three times ten is thirty routes through X. Fifty-six minus thirty is twenty-six. It matches!

lines.text: So when would you pick each way? Corner numbers work even with lots of blocked corners.
lines.caption: So when would you pick each way? Corner numbers work even with lots of blocked corners.

lines.text: Subtracting is the fastest when just one corner is blocked.
lines.caption: Subtracting is the fastest when just one corner is blocked.

lines.text: Choice C, thirty, counts every route that goes THROUGH X. Those are the ones to take away!
lines.caption: Choice C, thirty, counts every route that goes THROUGH X. Those are the ones to take away!

lines.text: Choice E, fifty-six, counts every route, and forgets about X.
lines.caption: Choice E, fifty-six, counts every route, and forgets about X.

lines.text: Thirty-five is what you'd get if you counted the grid as only four blocks wide.
lines.caption: Thirty-five is what you'd get if you counted the grid as only four blocks wide.

lines.text: Twenty is what a grid three blocks wide would give.
lines.caption: Twenty is what a grid three blocks wide would give.

lines.text: Watch out: don't add three and ten here. Fifty-six minus thirteen is forty-three, and that's not a choice.
lines.caption: Watch out: don't add three and ten here. Fifty-six minus thirteen is forty-three, and that's not a choice.

lines.text: So here's a great habit: count the blocks carefully, and check which routes you were asked for.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit: count the blocks carefully, and check which routes you were asked for.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: a four by four grid

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the grid is four blocks across and four blocks up.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the grid is four blocks across and four blocks up.

lines.text: Corner X is right in the middle. How many routes go from A to B without passing X?
lines.caption: Corner X is right in the middle. How many routes go from A to B without passing X?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's solve it by subtracting. Every route has four rights and four ups.
lines.caption: Let's solve it by subtracting. Every route has four rights and four ups.

lines.text: Eight times seven times six times five, over four times three times two times one, is seventy.
lines.caption: Eight times seven times six times five, over four times three times two times one, is seventy.

lines.text: Pick which two of the four steps go up: four times three is twelve, and each pair is counted twice, so six ways.
lines.caption: Pick which two of the four steps go up: four times three is twelve, and each pair is counted twice, so six ways.

lines.text: From X to B is six ways too. So six times six is thirty-six routes through X.
lines.caption: From X to B is six ways too. So six times six is thirty-six routes through X.

lines.text: Seventy minus thirty-six is thirty-four!
lines.caption: Seventy minus thirty-six is thirty-four!

lines.text: In the corner table, the zero in the middle wipes out every route through X.
lines.caption: In the corner table, the zero in the middle wipes out every route through X.

lines.text: The corner numbers give thirty-four as well. If you found it, amazing work!
lines.caption: The corner numbers give thirty-four as well. If you found it, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Count all the routes, then subtract the routes through the blocked corner.
lines.caption: Count all the routes, then subtract the routes through the blocked corner.

lines.text: Or fill in corner numbers: add the left and below, with a zero on the blocked corner.
lines.caption: Or fill in corner numbers: add the left and below, with a zero on the blocked corner.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
